clue.text: Hateful, but do turn over debts

indicators.note: to turn the word over is to flip it so it reads the other way

parts.note: taken as written before being flipped
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hateful to have to turn over their debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious arouses loathing, so it is hateful.

clue.text: Queries become such a gentleman

indicators.note: the letters of the word turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Questions are what a polite gentleman becomes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' tells you the letters of QUERIES change into a new word; 'such a' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An esquire is a title for a man of gentle birth, a gentleman.

clue.text: Royal Grandma who spent her life sailing

explanation.surface: A royal grandmother who lived her whole life at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Mary was the grandmother of Elizabeth II; a famous Cunard liner was named after her and spent its working life at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the consort of George V, a royal grandmother; the other is the ocean liner bearing her name.

clue.text: The essence of French motoring

parts.note: 'essence' is the French word for motor fuel, so the clue asks what drives a car in France

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what lies at the heart of driving in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essence' looks like 'core', but in French it is the fuel you put in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The French call motor fuel 'essence', so French motoring runs on it.

clue.text: Harry barged about

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone harried others and pushed their way around.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester or harass them, a synonym of harry.

clue.text: She is entitled to exclude one on points

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
taken as written
S and S are compass points, south twice

explanation.surface: A woman has the right to shut out a person on technicalities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' means holding a title, not having a right.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness holds a noble title, so she literally has a title.

clue.text: Dug up some tough cotton cloth

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: dug means mined

explanation.surface: Excavating some hard-wearing fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Figured at last, the Man and the Hour!

definitions.text: Figured at last, the Man and the Hour!

parts.words: Figured at last, the Man and the Hour!
parts.note: a figure that comes late, and the phrase for the last possible moment, the hour at the very end

explanation.surface: A grand announcement that the right man has arrived at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' points to the phrase for the final moment before it is too late, the 'eleventh hour'; 'figured' says the answer is a number word.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh hour is the last moment, and the ordinal number is a figure.

clue.text: The uneasiness felt when Pluto isn't making a sound

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
something silent is quiet

explanation.surface: Anxiety arises when the dog Pluto falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto suggests the planet or the cartoon dog; here it is the god of the underworld, also called Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: Disquiet is a feeling of anxiety or unease.

clue.text: First pilot meeting unusual danger crashed, RAF style

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken
the letters are made unusual by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A lead pilot meets odd danger and crashes his plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'RAF style' marks the definition as service slang; 'meeting' only joins the pilot's initial to the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: To prang an aircraft is RAF slang for crashing it.

clue.text: The germ of tomorrow's plant

parts.note: the part of a flower that, once fertilised, grows into a seed and a future plant

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the origin of a factory yet to be built.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure in a seed plant that develops into a seed after fertilisation.

clue.text: A peculiar figure nobody manages to pair off?

explanation.surface: An odd person no one can find a partner for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a person but is a number; an odd one cannot be split into pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd integer is a strange-sounding figure, and it cannot be divided into couples evenly.

clue.text: She comes out for the border rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden border

explanation.surface: A woman emerges for the garden border.
explanation.definitionFit: A deb, short for debutante, is a young woman making her formal entry into society.

clue.text: Mix-up with the motor cycle race

explanation.surface: A muddle at a motorbike event.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a hurried jumble, and also a cross-country motorbike race.

clue.text: Rakish Left splitting a little county

indicators.note: one piece forces the other apart by sitting in its middle

parts.note: Sy is a short form of Surrey, a county south of London
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A dashing politician of the Left divides a small county.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporty can mean flashy or jaunty in style, like rakish.

clue.text: Interest in stamps on a Greek letter recently

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lately means recently

explanation.surface: A new fascination with stamps bearing a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is the collecting and study of postage stamps.

clue.text: Cause confusion with advice to live more violently

parts.note: 'be' urges someone to exist, to live
wilder means more fierce or violent

explanation.surface: Telling someone to live more recklessly only causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone is to perplex or confuse them.

clue.text: Manipulate a clothing outfit

explanation.surface: Fiddling with a set of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig is to fix fraudulently; a rig is also an informal word for an outfit of clothing.

clue.text: An outburst of derision for one of Cromwell's men

indicators.note: the letters burst out and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Cromwell's soldiers greeted with mocking laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironsides were Oliver Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ironsides were the cavalry troopers under Cromwell, so one of them is a soldier of his.

clue.text: A silencer in evidence after firing

parts.note: sh is said to hush someone, silencing them

explanation.surface: A silenced gun leaves traces after being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silencer' suggests a gun attachment; it is the call 'sh!'. Firing burns things, leaving cinders.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdery residue is what remains after something has burned.

clue.text: A moving little Western air

parts.note: air in motion is wind, and a gentle one from the west has a classical name

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a touching short cowboy song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like a tune and 'Western' a film genre; it is a light breeze from the west.
explanation.definitionFit: A zephyr is a soft, mild breeze, named after the Greek god of the west wind.

clue.text: Slate vessel

explanation.surface: Criticising a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is to criticise harshly, the same as to pan; a pan is also a cooking vessel.

clue.text: This very weak person is having no effect

explanation.surface: A frail person whose efforts change nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An invalid is someone infirm through illness; invalid also means void, without force.

clue.text: High-flown transport getting fifty in drier circles

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: an airer is a frame for drying clothes
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Transport getting fifty people up into drier skies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drier' is not a comparative here but a noun: a clothes airer, the frame that dries washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger aircraft flies high, a lofty mode of transport.

clue.text: A sure way to start a flare-up?

definitions.text: A sure way to start a flare-up?

parts.words: A sure way to start a flare-up?
parts.note: a flare-up sounds like a quarrel but literally is a burst of flame, which needs setting alight

explanation.surface: Seems to ask how to provoke an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to set fire to it, beginning a blaze.

clue.text: Change from evil past or heartless present

indicators.note: the middle of the word is removed, leaving only its outer parts

parts.note: to represent is to present or depict

explanation.surface: Advice to give up a wicked past or a cruel present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes RES from the middle of REPRESENT; 'or' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel remorse and turn away from former sins.

clue.text: By Jove! Flash Harry's head tingling excitedly!

indicators.note: the letters jump around excitedly into a new order
the leading letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An exclamation as dashing Flash Harry gets a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes H from 'Harry's' and 'excitedly' mixes it with TINGLING. Jove, king of the gods, hurled thunderbolts.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash from the sky is a bolt, the weapon of Jupiter (Jove).

clue.text: How to give the couple one's fair share

definitions.text: How to give the couple one's fair share

parts.words: How to give the couple one's fair share
parts.note: for two people to share fairly, something must be split exactly in two

explanation.surface: Seems to ask how a pair gets what is due to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To split something into two equal parts gives each of a pair the same portion.

clue.text: A heavy walk for a vagrant

explanation.surface: A long trudge for a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long tiring walk, and also a homeless wanderer.

clue.text: Deputy Lieutenant icily turned to description of rustic innocence

indicators.note: the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: DL is the abbreviation for Deputy Lieutenant, a county official in Britain

explanation.surface: A county official coldly turns to pastoral writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll depicts peaceful country life, so idyllic describes such simple pastoral charm.

clue.text: Such a horse could be last jungle king

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the lion is called king of the jungle

explanation.surface: A horse might be the final ruler of the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: A 20 block?

parts.note: 20 is the light wind at 20-across; a light wind is a word that precedes 'block' in a building material

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about obstructing the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: A breeze block is a lightweight building block made from cinders and cement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle wind like the one at 20 is a light breeze, and breeze blocks are building bricks.
